nodes.text:
Set an isolated Egyptian temple ruin within a vast, softly rolling orange desert. Make one compact rectangular temple the dominant structure, with a flat, nearly complete slab roof bounded by uneven pale stone coping. Keep the three elevations other than the entrance mostly solid and monumental, repeating rectangular relief panels and horizontal ornamental courses across them.

Face its decorated entrance onto an open forecourt. Use a broad, shadowed central opening, several closely spaced papyrus-style columns with colorful flared capitals, shorter square supports, and low painted railings; through these, reveal a dark columned interior and a faintly illuminated passage beyond. Build the massive walls from pale sandstone, slightly battered and divided by shallow projecting sections. Detail them with engraved panels, faded figures and hieroglyphic bands, thin gold accents, and painted friezes in turquoise, yellow, red, and blue.

In front of the temple and slightly off to one side, place a detached colonnade's remains. Set four tall, slender painted columns in a loose line beneath two offset, incomplete sandstone lintel beams, maintaining obvious gaps and broken continuity. Around the column bases, scatter small fragments and cracked paving slabs into an irregular trail, partly buried in sand.
